title: Active-River current-boundary admission and next-boundary management memory

sequencing.rationale: Freeze the two-day active-exchange memory prediction before observing DUMMY-20H active-case runtime output.

current_boundary_pending.use: execution dependency only; no DUMMY-20H runtime values were used to derive the frozen reference

frozen_model.active_river_sample_and_hold: At each 6-hour product-step start use accepted Basin/subgrid level as River stage; hold resulting MF6 River flux through the following Ribasim segment.

derivation: Use the qualified DUMMY-20G effective River relation q_riv = 15.999829335153766 * (h_stage - 0.5) m3/day.
Use Ribasim v2026.1.1 UserDemand reduction phi(x)=(-2*x_s+3)*x_s^2 for 0<x<0.02, x_s=x/0.02.
At t=0 priority-1 level hold and active River forcing leave 32-q_riv(1.0)=24.000085332423117 m3/day for root-first allocation.
Integrate each 6-hour physical segment with River flux held at the segment-start accepted stage.
At t=24h fixed allocation.dt re-solves from accepted excess storage, fixed supply and current River forcing over the next one-day management interval.

hypotheses: DUMMY-20I reproduces the DUMMY-20H one-day active-River prefix within tolerance.
The t=0 allocation is approximately 24.0000853/0 m3/day root/external.
External physical delivery remains zero throughout day 1.
Accepted physical state accumulates approximately 11.9892 m3 excess Basin storage by t=24 h despite continuous active-River loss.
At the t=24 h fixed allocation boundary, the new root allocation rises prospectively to approximately 35.9891 m3/day while external allocation remains zero.
The new day-2 allocation affects only physical realization after t=24 h.
Active-River flux remains reciprocal to Ribasim infiltration and changes with accepted Basin stage at each 6-hour boundary.
The source = root + external + active-River transfer + Basin-storage ledger closes at every accepted boundary.
forbidden: no use of DUMMY-20H observed values to retune the frozen hybrid reference
no inference beyond the qualified two-cell active-River topology
